summary: Rumney, NH summit tower: 16-ft wooden tower 1911, 27-ft steel tower 1927, WMNF operation from 1939, removed 1985; trails reach the summit and foundations were reported.

facts.design: 16-foot wooden tower (1911), then a 27-foot steel tower (1927)
facts.status_note: Dismantled and removed in 1985 according to a summit display; a winter trip report describes concrete foundations still visible

access.note: Hiking and snowmobile trails reach the summit from a trailhead on Lower Doetown Road; there is no tower to climb

visit.trail_note: Trailhead on Lower Doetown Road (start of FR 413); one trail for hikers and one for snowmobilers to the summit

facts.agency: Built by the NH Timberland Owners; operated by the White Mountain National Forest from 1939

events.note: 16-foot wooden tower, one of six built by the NH Timberland Owners, per a summit display quoted in a trip report
27-foot steel tower, per the same summit display
White Mountain National Forest took over operation of three towers, Stinson Mountain included, from the State Forestry Department
Frank Woodward of Rumney officially occupied the tower on April 13 for the first time that year
Tower remained in service until after 1967, per the summit display
Dismantled and removed, per the summit display

evidence.supports: Stinson Mountain is in Grafton County, New Hampshire
the mountain stands above Stinson Lake; its fire tower and ski trail are gone
evidence.quote: Standing above Stinson Lake, Stinson Mountain once featured a fire tower and ski trail, both of which are gone.

evidence.supports: the summit display says the first tower was established in 1911 by the NH Timberland Owners as a 16-foot wooden tower
evidence.quote: Established in 1911, one of 6 towers constructed by the NH Timberland Owners, it was a 16’ wooden tower.

evidence.supports: a 27-foot steel tower was built in 1927
evidence.quote: in 1927 a 27’ steel tower was built

evidence.supports: in 1939 the White Mountain National Forest took over operation of three towers from the State Forestry Department (item dated August 3, 1939), Stinson Mountain in Rumney among them
evidence.quote: Operation of three borderline towers has recently been taken over from the State Forestry Department by the White Mountain National Forest

evidence.supports: Frank Woodward of Rumney officially occupied the tower on April 13, 1941, for the first time that year (item dated April 25, 1941)
evidence.quote: Lookout towerman Frank Woodward of Rumney officially occupied the Stinson Mountain Fire Tower Sunday, April 13 for the first time this year.

evidence.supports: the tower remained in service until after 1967 and was dismantled and removed in 1985
evidence.quote: It remained in service until after 1967, and was dismantled and removed in 1985.

evidence.supports: the Forest Lookouts entry marks the tower as removed
the summit has one trail for hikers and one for snowmobilers
evidence.quote: There is currently two trails to the summit - one for hikers and one for snowmobilers.

evidence.supports: the hike begins at a trailhead on Lower Doetown Road
evidence.quote: Beginning the hike at the standard trailhead on Lower Doetown Road

evidence.supports: a winter trip report describes concrete foundations still visible through deep snow near the summit
evidence.quote: On this wintery day, the old fire tower concrete foundations were visible through the deep snow

evidence.supports: the ski history page lists the summit ski trail under the White Mountain National Forest
the New Hampshire lookout list marks the Stinson Mountain tower as gone
the 1939 item was printed in the Portsmouth Herald
the 1941 item appeared in the Groton Times
the summit display, quoted in the trip report
evidence.quote: Even a small display stands atop the mountain to showcase some of Stinson's prior fire lookout history

sources.title: Stinson Mountain, New Hampshire - New England's Alpine CCC Ski Trails

notes_for_editor: The 1911 and 1927 dates and the 1985 removal come from a single summit display as quoted in one trip report (A Talk in the Woods); the trip report's date is not in the text read. The 1939 and 1941 items are newspaper extracts reproduced on the Forest Lookouts page; the originals were not read. The state fire tower history PDF (nhdfl.dncr.nh.gov) returned HTTP 403 and was not used. No photos were added. Brief record (gone, tower) confirmed; no corrections proposed.
